title: tanacetum cadmeum
intro: Tanacetum cadmeum, commonly known as Mountain Feverfew, is a perennial plant in the daisy family (Asteraceae) that is native to the mountainous regions of Greece. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include reducing fever, relieving headaches, and easing digestive issues due to its anti-inflammatory and antispasmodic properties. The therapeutic actions of Tanacetum cadmeum include calming the nervous system, reducing inflammation, and exhibiting antimicrobial activity. The bioactive constituents of the plant include flavonoids, terpenoids, and sesquiterpenes, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
